name: Dusty puce
lede: Dusty puce is a soft, greyed pink-brown taken from Sakuranezumi, a Japanese traditional color name meaning cherry blossom mouse grey.

sections.title: Cherry blossom mouse grey
sections.body:
Our library files this hue under Sakuranezumi, written 桜鼠, one of the traditional Japanese color names Wikipedia's "Traditional colors of Japan" list carries [1]. The kanji combine cherry blossom and mouse, naming a pink softened toward the grey of a mouse's coat [1]. Our conversion to the ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary calls the nearest block "light grayish red," about 3.1 units of ΔE away [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[deep-vinaceous]] and [[antique-rose]], at Among the other Japanese-named hues in our data it sits near [[dusty-wine]] and [[dusty-sepia]], both darker and browner [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match to Dusty puce in 87 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.37 percent, as photographed [2]. It is rarer than roughly half the named colors we track, and plays a hidden color, tucked into shadow rather than light, in just over half of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 7 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.1 times the archive's overall rate for that century, and is somewhat over-represented in paintings from India [2]. The earliest dated match in our data is the year 1000, far earlier than any record of the name itself, so it marks a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not a dated use of the color's name, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not a pigment identification [2].
